articles.title: 'We haven't ruled it out...': Markwayne Mullin leaves cyberattack theory open in US aviation outage
articles.description: US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Friday (local time) said authorities had found no evidence so far that a telecommunications outage which triggered a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop was caused by a cyberattack or rogue artificial intelligence, but stressed that investigators were not ruling out any possibility. Responding to whether he could say with 100 per cent certainty that the disruption was not caused by a cyberattack or rogue AI, Mullin said the available evidence pointed towards a mechanical failure, although investigations were continuing. 'There's nothing completely certain right now. It doesn't appear that way. We've activated our teams...This is a national emergency. We have all of our assets...There is nothing that indicates it yet,' Mullin said.

articles.title: Tired of paying for cloud storage every month? pCloud’s Black Friday Lifetime deal is the cure for subscription fatigue
articles.description: Software used to be a one-time purchase, but over time, with the addition of cloud storage and services, everything has become a subscription. One company even tried to make your car seat heaters a subscription. Count the subscriptions you’re paying for right now: iCloud, a password manager, a couple of streaming services, a music service, maybe a VPN, and whatever other app decided this year that it needed to be $4.99 per month for something that used to be a one-time purchase. Everything is a service now, and a lot of people are hitting the point where one more monthly charge is one too many on principle alone.
